phase: The errand becomes an appointment. As an optional need the model did it ten times in a hundred; as a work duty the same model turns up ninety-two times in a hundred. daily_resource_contract refuses a mandatory need outright, so this uses the object work already uses - required_activities with a time, a place and evidence in the citizen's own text. All 480 cells got one and all sampled grammars build.
primary: Paired per-citizen composition distance against the v18 v25 arm, resampling citizens. Success is a 95% interval that excludes zero on the closer side. The same test on v34 gave -0.0198 [-0.0855, +0.0405], so a difference under about 0.06 cannot be told apart at this roster size.
limitations: The scenario fixes that an errand exists, its category, its hour and its place. It does not fix what is bought, how much, or whether the policy changes it - that is what DS-1 measures.

The hour is chosen mechanically outside every fixed duty with the citizen's own commute as clearance, so workers get an evening slot and non-workers an afternoon one. That is a systematic difference between the two groups, not a random one.
An appointment the model cannot keep becomes a contract failure rather than a skipped need, so the valid rate is a cancellation criterion rather than a background number.
preflight: 277 unit checks passed including 6 new resource-gate regressions. Source, v25 and asset_transaction_v7 unchanged from the previous round.
selection: Closed pair carried from v16/v17 (experiments/v18/prompt_v18.md). No new candidate.
